title: The opposite-category involution of the infinity category of infinity categories
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets, cores, equivalences and universes from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of quasicategories in a fixed universe, with the cores of their functor simplicial sets as mapping spaces, from [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration]. For a simplicial set $K$ let $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ have the same sets of $n$-simplices, the operator of a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ on $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ being the operator of $\alpha^\vee:[m]\to[n]$, $\alpha^\vee(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$, on $K$; a simplicial map $f:K\to L$ has $f^{\mathrm{op}}:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to L^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the same components. Then $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory whenever $C$ is, $(K^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=K$, and $(K\times L)^{\mathrm{op}}=K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L^{\mathrm{op}}$. There is a coherent functor $\mathrm{op}:\mathrm{Cat}_\infty\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, including all higher simplices, whose value on an object $C$ is $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and whose value on an arrow, a functor $u:C\to D$, is $u^{\mathrm{op}}:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$, together with a natural equivalence $\mathrm{op}\circ\mathrm{op}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}$ of coherent functors whose component at each $C$ is equivalent to the identity of $(C^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=C$. In particular $\mathrm{op}$ is an equivalence of infinity categories. The same holds for $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ formed in any larger universe, compatibly with the inclusion of the smaller one.

source.place: Section 1.2.1 (the opposite of a simplicial set and of an infinity category); the coherent involution of the infinity category of infinity categories: B. Toen, Vers une axiomatisation de la theorie des categories superieures, K-Theory 34 (2005), Section 6. Neither is in literature/; WANTED by the Q115 maintainer reader. Used in step 1 of lem-coef-ind-right-adjoint-coherent to make C -> Fun(C^op, S) a coherent contravariant functor.

proof.text: For composable monotone maps $\alpha:[l]\to[m]$ and $\beta:[m]\to[n]$, $(\beta\alpha)^\vee(i)=n-\beta(\alpha(l-i))=(\beta^\vee\alpha^\vee)(i)$, and $(1)^\vee=1$. Thus the stated operators define a simplicial set and make $f\mapsto f^{\mathrm{op}}$ a covariant functor on simplicial sets. The formulas $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$ and coordinatewise action on products give $(K^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=K$ and $(K\times L)^{\mathrm{op}}=K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L^{\mathrm{op}}$, on operators as well as simplices.

source.place: Section 1.2.1; explicit calculation of the opposite simplex operators.

proof.text: The map $\theta_n:\Delta^n\to(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ sending a $k$-simplex $\gamma:[k]\to[n]$ to $\gamma^\vee$ is an isomorphism and sends face $i$ to face $n-i$. Applying opposite to $\Lambda_i^n\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and using $\theta_n$ therefore gives a map $\Lambda_{n-i}^n\to C$. Since $0<n-i<n$, it has a filler; applying the inverse reversal gives the required filler in $C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence opposite preserves quasicategories. Reversing an edge, its inverse, and the two inverse-witnessing triangles gives inverse witnesses in the opposite, so an edge is an equivalence if and only if its opposite is.

source.place: Section 1.2.1, reversed horn indices; inverse-edge definition in def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones.

proof.text: Use the marked simplicial sets, marking conventions, products and $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}$ of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. For $X=(K,M)$ set $O(X)=(K^{\mathrm{op}},M)$, identifying the degree-one sets, and set $O(f)=f^{\mathrm{op}}$. This preserves degeneracies and marked maps, and $O^2=\mathrm{id}$; Step 2 gives $O(C^\natural)=(C^{\mathrm{op}})^\natural$. For an $n$-simplex $h:X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Y$ of $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(X,Y)$, put $\rho_n(h)=h^{\mathrm{op}}\circ(1\times\theta_n)$. The identity $\theta_n\alpha=(\alpha^\vee)^{\mathrm{op}}\theta_m$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ gives $\rho_n(h)\circ(1\times\alpha)=\rho_m(h\circ(1\times\alpha^\vee))$. Thus the actual natural simplicial isomorphism is $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(X,Y)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(OX,OY)$, with an opposite on the source. Applying the formula twice is identity.

source.place: Sections 1.2.1 and 3.1.3: Map-sharp defined before Remark 3.1.3.1; explicit operator calculation (agent expansion).

proof.text:
For any simplicial set $A$, define $r_A:|A^{\mathrm{op}}|	o|A|$ by $[a,(t_0,\ldots,t_n)]\mapsto[a,(t_n,\ldots,t_0)]$, using the realization quotient of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. For a simplex operator $\alpha:[m]	o[n]$, barycentric reflection satisfies $r_n\alpha_*=(\alpha^\vee)_*r_m$, so this formula respects every quotient relation. It is continuous on each simplex, natural in $A$, and its inverse is the identical reflection for $A^{\mathrm{op}}$. Hence a simplicial map is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if its opposite is. For a marked weak equivalence $f:X	o Y$ and any quasicategory $C$, Step 3 identifies the test map $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(OY,C^
atural)	o\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(OX,C^
atural)$ with the opposite of $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Y,(C^{\mathrm{op}})^
atural)	o\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(X,(C^{\mathrm{op}})^
atural)$. This is a weak homotopy equivalence by the defining test in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], since $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. Therefore $O$ preserves marked weak equivalences.

source.place: Sections 1.2.1 and 3.1.3, weak-equivalence test; quotient-reflection proof written by the second reader.

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal M$ be the marked model category over a point from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], with weak equivalences $W$, and let $\mathcal F$ be its ordinary full subcategory on $C^
atural$. That node makes every object cofibrant, identifies the fibrant objects with these $C^
atural$, and identifies their enriched mapping sets with $\operatorname{Fun}(C,D)^\simeq$, compatibly with composition. Thus its bifibrant coherent nerve is exactly the $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration]. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]: the canonical functor $q:N(\mathcal F)	o\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, sending $C^
atural$ to $C$ and a strict functor $u$ to its corresponding edge, is a homotopy coherent localization at $W|_{\mathcal F}$. In particular restriction along $q$ identifies entire functor infinity categories with the full subcategories inverting these weak equivalences, for arbitrary target infinity categories, not just their homotopy categories.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Remark 1.3.4.16; HTT Definition 3.0.0.1 and Corollary 3.1.4.4 identify the marked-point model.

proof.text: By Steps 2-4, $O$ restricts to an ordinary endofunctor of $\mathcal F$ preserving $W|_{\mathcal F}$. Therefore $qN(O)$ inverts that class. The full functor-category universal property in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] extends it to a coherent functor $\mathrm{op}:\mathrm{Cat}_\infty\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, with specified natural equivalence $\eta:\mathrm{op}\,q\simeq qN(O)$. On $q(C^\natural)=C$ and $q(u)=u$, this comparison identifies its object and arrow values with $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $u^{\mathrm{op}}$, respectively. Because this is an equivalence of entire functor infinity categories, the extension includes every higher simplex and its composition coherences. No simplicial map between the unopposed core mapping sets is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20, homotopy coherent localization universal property; explicit application to the ordinary relative functor O.

proof.text: Restrict $\mathrm{op}^2$ along $q$ and compose the comparisons $\mathrm{op}(\eta)$ and $\eta N(O)$ to obtain $\mathrm{op}^2q\simeq qN(O)^2=q$. Full faithfulness of restriction along $q$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] lifts this specified equivalence to $\epsilon:\mathrm{op}^2\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Cat}_\infty}$. After the specified identifications of the two successive object values, its component at $C$ is the identity of $(C^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=C$, because the restricted comparison ends with the strict identity $O^2=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\mathrm{op}$ is its own two-sided inverse and is an equivalence in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20, full faithfulness on coherent natural transformations; the double-op comparison is written out here.

proof.text: All opposite operators, marked products and the reflection maps are given in the universe of the input simplicial sets. The marked-point model and its bifibrant description are universe-relative by [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. For universes $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal V$, let $i:\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal U}\to\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal V}$ be the natural inclusion. The two functors $i\,\mathrm{op}_{\mathcal U}$ and $\mathrm{op}_{\mathcal V}i$ restrict along $q_{\mathcal U}$ to the same $q_{\mathcal V}N(O)$ on the smaller ordinary category of fibrant objects. Apply the full faithfulness in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] with target $\mathrm{Cat}_{\infty,\mathcal V}$ to obtain their natural equivalence; their double-op comparisons agree because both restrict to $O^2=\mathrm{id}$. This is the claimed compatibility with universe inclusion.
